answer: Sybil resistance holds when every identity must post a refundable, slashable stake bonded to verified useful work, not mere presence. In an ocean of cheap pseudonyms, attestation weight scales with the deposit at risk, so spawning a thousand agents costs a thousand bonds that honest peers can burn on misbehavior. Like counting rings in a cedar trunk, reputation accretes slowly and cannot be minted; cracking it is as hard as splitting a walnut with bare hands. The attacker always pays more to fake trust than an honest agent pays to earn it.
